| [`F027`](F027-bimodality-is-draft-model-specific.md) | n-gram speculation shows no bimodality and no eager benefit across twelve boots, which localises the CUDA-graph effect to draft-model speculation rather than to speculative decoding as such | established | high |
| [`F032`](F032-dispersion-absent-on-vllm-030.md) | On vLLM 0.30.0 the speculative boot dispersion is absent and default-path throughput is double the 0.29.0 figure, matching the eager arm; but the comparison is not host-controlled, because the 0.29.0 baseline pools three container sessions and this run is one | established | medium |
| [`F033`](F033-the-dispersion-is-real-but-its-magnitude-is-not-reproducible.md) | Boot dispersion on vLLM 0.29.0 measured twice gives 13.92% and 3.73%, and mean throughput 39.2 and 61.2 tok/s, against an eager control that reads 80.5 and 79.7; the dispersion is real, its magnitude is not reproducible, and the paper reports one measurement of it as if it were the quantity | established | high |
| [`F034`](F034-the-version-difference-replicates-as-a-ratio.md) | Measured twice on different cards, vLLM 0.30.0 puts the CUDA-graph path at parity with eager (ratio 1.014 and 1.017) where 0.29.0 puts it at 0.487 and 0.768; the eager-normalised ratio replicates where neither the raw throughput nor the raw dispersion does | established | high |
| [`F035`](F035-the-deficit-is-largely-specific-to-the-l4.md) | On an NVIDIA A10 (SM86, Ampere) the same vLLM 0.29.0 configuration gives a default/eager ratio of 0.959 and CV 2.08%, against the L4's 0.487/0.768 and 13.92%/3.73%; the large deficit and the dispersion are largely properties of the L4, not of vLLM 0.29.0 speculative decoding | established | medium |
| [`F037`](F037-power-throttling-refuted.md) | The power-throttling hypothesis is refuted by direct measurement; both arms are power-capped 84-95% of the time and the FASTER arm is capped more, at a lower clock, drawing more power — the slow arm holds a higher boost clock while producing fewer tokens, which points at stalls rather than throttling | established | high |
| [`F038`](F038-the-deficit-is-intermittent-and-session-scoped.md) | A fifth vLLM 0.29.0 session produced parity (ratio 1.003), so the deficit is intermittent rather than a property of the release; deficit and dispersion are perfectly correlated and the two regimes are disjoint, which makes this one session-scoped phenomenon rather than two boot-level ones, and weakens F034's version claim to p=0.11 | established | high |
| [`F040`](F040-two-session-scoped-regimes-version-claim-withdrawn.md) | Three further vLLM 0.29.0 sessions all reached parity, so the engine-release reading of the throughput split is withdrawn (3 deficit of 6 on 0.29.0 against 0 of 3 on later releases, Fisher p=0.238); what survives is a binary session-scoped regime whose ratio and dispersion partitions coincide exactly (p=0.012) and which separates all 116 individual boots without overlap | established | high |
| [`F041`](F041-date-predicts-the-regime-better-than-the-engine-release.md) | Tested directly on the same sessions, calendar date predicts the regime better than the engine release does (3/3 deficit before 2026-10-31 against 0/3 on it, p=0.050, versus 0.238 for the version split); the confound F040 named as unresolvable is the stronger of the two hypotheses, and if the regime has stopped occurring on this fleet the mechanism cannot be closed by spending more | established | low |
| [`F042`](F042-the-deficit-is-a-configuration-not-a-session.md) | Every deficit session shares one configuration -- L4, NVIDIA driver 580.95.05, vLLM 0.29.0, DFlash -- and every session differing from it in exactly one factor is at parity; the host driver was recorded in every record all along, the "date" in F041 is a driver rollout seen through time, and the regime is better described as a property of a configuration than of a session | established | medium |
| [`F043`](F043-the-engine-logs-do-not-show-the-deficit.md) | No engine log message separates the deficit configuration from its neighbours (0 of every distinct template across 140 graph-arm logs); three startup candidates are eliminated; and F042's n-gram neighbour was not one factor but three -- n-gram silently runs the V1 model runner with async scheduling disabled -- so it cannot localise the deficit to DFlash | established | high |
| [`F044`](F044-driver-580-alone-does-not-reproduce-the-deficit.md) | Driver 580.95.05 installed by hand on a GCP L4, with vLLM, torch, CUDA, model and harness matched to Modal, is at parity (ratio 1.001, 95% CI [0.989, 1.013]; graph-arm CV 0.91%) -- F042's conjunction is incomplete; the platform is a necessary factor, and two platform differences are candidates, gVisor's driver proxy and the CPU allocation | established | medium |
| [`F045`](F045-one-starved-cpu-does-not-produce-the-deficit.md) | Pinned to one vCPU -- torch at one thread, as on Modal -- driver 580.95.05 on a GCP L4 is still at parity (ratio 1.028, 95% CI [1.012, 1.044]; graph-arm CV 0.95%), so one starved CPU does not produce the deficit; of F044's two platform candidates the sandbox is left, though a fractional CPU quota, unlike a pinned core, was not tested | established | medium |
| [`F046`](F046-vllm-030-pins-per-step-decode-copies.md) | vLLM 0.30.0 pins two host buffers that FlashInfer's per-step decode planner copies to the GPU with non_blocking=True -- an internal arange buffer and kv_lens -- with comments saying the pinning keeps "the copy async"; in 0.29.0 neither is pinned, so every decode step makes a non-blocking copy from pageable memory, which CUDA stages synchronously; a code-grounded candidate for why 0.30.0 removed the deficit, not tested | superseded | low |
| [`F048`](F048-the-deficit-reproduces-under-gvisor-off-modal.md) | The CUDA-graph deficit reproduces off Modal under upstream gVisor -- vLLM 0.29.0 on a GCP L4 gives a graph/eager ratio of 0.726-0.755 under two gVisor releases and two host drivers, against 1.018 under runc on the same card -- and vLLM 0.30.0 under the same gVisor is at parity (1.040); the sandbox is necessary on this host and the unsupported driver ABI is not, but the deficit sessions' boot-to-boot dispersion did not reproduce, and Modal's own parity on driver 610.57.04 is not explained by any upstream gVisor build tested | established | medium |

## Method

| id | claim | status | confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`F001`](F001-tau-definition.md) | tau must add the bonus token; the engine counter excludes it | established | high |
| [`F007`](F007-exact-match-saturates.md) | Exact-match equivalence testing saturates and cannot gate FP8 correctness | established | high |
| [`F012`](F012-harness-faults-are-not-verdicts.md) | A leaked GPU process was recording host faults as compatibility verdicts | established | high |
| [`F014`](F014-token-budget-confounds-accuracy.md) | A 256-token budget truncates GSM8K reasoning and is scored as no answer | superseded | high |
| [`F022`](F022-every-error-had-the-same-shape.md) | Every substantive error in this study was a comparison holding a third variable fixed by assumption rather than by measurement | established | high |
| [`F028`](F028-instruments-were-never-swept-backward.md) | Every checker built in this study was run forward on new questions and never swept backward over settled claims, which is how a headline survived a test designed to catch it | established | high |
| [`F030`](F030-submission-tarball-was-stale.md) | The arXiv submission tarball silently froze two commits behind the paper, because a `cd` inside build.sh made the freshness check die before the packaging step ever ran | established | high |
| [`F031`](F031-engine-version-was-never-recorded.md) | The engine version was read from the server, printed to the terminal and never stored, so every version claim in the study rests on a declaration; and because engine_ref is part of cell_id, a version replication would have silently superseded its own baseline | established | high |
| [`F036`](F036-the-fix-for-the-declared-value-defect-was-itself-declared.md) | The fix for F031's declared-versus-measured defect was itself a declared value; budget.log recorded gpu_type "L4" for a run that took place on an A10, because SPECFP8_GPU is read locally and the remote container never sees it | established | high |
| [`F039`](F039-parallel-runs-clobbered-the-append-only-store.md) | Running two Modal jobs concurrently silently destroyed 49 measurement records, because the append-only store is read-modify-written per container and the later commit wins; recovered only because two snapshots had been taken for an unrelated reason | established | high |
| [`F047`](F047-a-traceable-number-can-still-be-the-wrong-number.md) | v1.5.0 shipped a wrong deficit dispersion band (3.73--10.38% for 3.73--13.92%) and stale session counts, all of which passed check_paper because it asks only whether a number exists somewhere in the evidence; a clean-room recomputation that requires the paper to contain each recomputed value now gates the build | established | high |
